Framework: EU AI Act (Reg. 2024/1689, as amended by the Digital Omnibus on AI)
What Triggers It: Placing an AI system on the EU market, or the system output being used in the EU, regardless of where the provider sits
Overlap or Conflict: Annex III high-risk obligations apply from 2 December 2027; Annex I from 2 August 2028. Article 50 transparency duties and the Article 4 AI literacy duty were not postponed. Credit scoring is an Annex III use case, so a LatAm lending model with any EU customer exposure is in scope.

What Triggers It: Adopted by choice, or required by a US enterprise customer through contract
Overlap or Conflict: Maps closely to ISO/IEC 42001 controls. Using both means one control set with two label systems, not two programs. US federal financial-sector guidance builds on it.

What Triggers It: An AI component that takes autonomous action: calls an API, writes data, triggers a workflow
Overlap or Conflict: Covers action authority and tool invocation security, which general AI RMF does not. An agent is not covered adequately by a model-level control set.

What Triggers It: Certification decision, usually driven by enterprise procurement rather than regulation
Overlap or Conflict: The management-system shell that a regulator-facing audit can hang on. Certification proves the process exists, not that any specific system is safe.

What Triggers It: Performing an AI system impact assessment
Overlap or Conflict: Gives structure to the impact assessment that the EU AI Act and Brazil's PL 2338 both require in substance. Useful as the shared template across jurisdictions.

What Triggers It: Processing personal data of individuals in Brazil, or offering goods and services to them
Overlap or Conflict: Article 20 gives a right to review of automated decisions. That right is live today, with no AI statute needed. ANPD is the enforcing authority.

What Triggers It: Would apply on enactment to providers and operators of AI systems affecting people in Brazil
Overlap or Conflict: Approved by the Senate in December 2024, still with the Chamber of Deputies as of August 2026. Risk-based structure modeled on the EU AI Act. Coordination sits with ANPD under a distributed sectoral model.

What Triggers It: Processing personal data held by private parties in Mexico
Overlap or Conflict: A new statute effective 21 March 2025, not an amendment. INAI was dissolved; enforcement moved to the Secretariat of Anti-Corruption and Good Governance. Adds accountability for automated decision-making. Privacy notices referencing INAI are stale.

What Triggers It: Processing personal data of individuals in Colombia
Overlap or Conflict: Enforced by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio. Database registration in the RNBD is an operational obligation that is easy to miss during market entry.

What Triggers It: Public-sector AI programs and sector regulator expectations
Overlap or Conflict: Sets direction rather than obligations. Colombia governs AI through the data protection statute and sector supervision, so the binding constraint is Law 1581 plus SFC circulars.

What Triggers It: Meeting the California revenue or data-volume thresholds and handling California resident data
Overlap or Conflict: CPPA rules on automated decision-making technology add obligations on top of the base statute; confirm the current compliance dates before scoping. Other US state privacy statutes differ enough that a single US posture is a simplification.

What Triggers It: Storing, processing or transmitting cardholder data anywhere in the flow
Overlap or Conflict: Enforced through card network agreements, not law, which means the deadline is the acquirer's and there is no regulatory grace period. Scope creeps quietly when logs or support tooling touch PAN data.

What Triggers It: Cross-border transfer requiring originator and beneficiary information to travel with the payment
Overlap or Conflict: Implemented differently in each market and on different timelines. Directly connected to the ISO 20022 structured address work, since the data quality the travel rule assumes is the data the address change forces.

Framework: National AML regimes: BSA (US), LFPIORPI (MX), Law 9.613/1998 (BR), SARLAFT (CO)
What Triggers It: Operating as a regulated financial institution or a designated non-financial obligated entity
Overlap or Conflict: Four supervisors with four reporting formats: FinCEN, the CNBV and UIF, COAF, and the UIAF under SFC rules. Screening logic can be shared. Reporting cannot.

What Triggers It: Being a non-bank financial institution under FTC jurisdiction holding US customer information
Overlap or Conflict: Prescribes named security program elements. Overlaps heavily with PCI DSS controls while using different vocabulary for the same measures.

What Triggers It: Being a US bank or bank holding company using models in decisions
Overlap or Conflict: Predates the AI vocabulary and still governs. A credit model called AI is a model under SR 11-7 first, whatever the AI governance program calls it.
